steps: Open the public GitLab entry page.
Browse or search public projects.
Open a project and inspect its repository, commits, branches, releases, and metadata.
Apply an impossible search and recover through the all-projects route.
Register a local developer account with required identity fields.
Read the local-only verification message and verify the account.
Open the authenticated dashboard and profile.
Sign out and sign back in with the local credentials.
Create a project with description, visibility, README, ignore template, and license.
Refresh its project page and verify the repository persists.
Open an owned project repository.
Create or edit a file and enter a commit message.
Verify the file, commit, and branch head persist after navigation.
Create a branch and inspect its comparison with the default branch.
Create an issue with labels, assignee, and milestone.
Comment on and close the issue.
Open a merge request between two branches and assign a reviewer.
Review its changes and discussion, then update its status.
Open the project pipeline list.
Trigger a deterministic local pipeline.
Inspect job status and logs.
Retry the pipeline without contacting a runner or source service.
Open project members and invite an existing local account with a selected role.
Change project topics, default branch, notifications, visibility, or archive state.
Verify an unauthorized role receives an access-denied response.
Open a public project and inspect its local clone and source-download affordances.
Fork it into the authenticated local namespace.
Verify the fork retains repository history without a remote request.
Open password recovery and submit a local account address.
Repeat the request and reuse the active flow without issuing another message.
Verify and replace the password through the local-only message.
Open a missing deep link and return safely to project discovery.
